_comment: Copyright 2026 Doug Trier. SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0. Windows term -> Trier Bridge route -> Linux reality. Every non-exact mapping carries a note (TB-INV-065). Routes: section (Trier Bridge view), gnome-settings (panel), folder (XDG folder key or URI), app (desktop id), teach (explanation only).

concepts.title: Task Manager
concepts.linux: Process and resource information from the kernel (procfs) and systemd
concepts.note: On Linux, apps, background processes, and services are separate things; not every process is an app.

concepts.title: Startup Apps
concepts.linux: Autostart entries in ~/.config/autostart and user systemd units
concepts.note: Linux has several startup mechanisms; Trier Bridge shows the ones it can see and says which is which.

concepts.title: Event Viewer
concepts.note: Linux has no Windows event IDs or channels; familiar categories are views over the journal.

concepts.title: Device Manager
concepts.note: Most drivers are part of the Linux kernel; there is no generic Update Driver button.

concepts.title: Disk Management
concepts.linux: udisks2 and the kernel block layer; GNOME Disks for changes
concepts.note: Linux mounts drives into folders instead of drive letters; formatting and partitioning stay in GNOME Disks.

concepts.title: Network Connections
concepts.note: Connections are profiles managed by NetworkManager; an adapter can have several.

concepts.title: Services
concepts.note: Running and enabled-at-boot are separate states on Linux; Trier Bridge never merges them.

concepts.title: Command Prompt
concepts.linux: Trier Bridge Terminal in Bridge Mode (Windows commands and PowerShell names become typed operations); real PowerShell opens in a terminal window when installed
concepts.note: Windows commands are understood as intent, not passed to a shell. Unknown commands do nothing.

concepts.title: System Information
concepts.linux: os-release, the kernel, logind, and the system bus

concepts.title: Installed Apps
concepts.linux: Packages from the distribution (apt), snaps, and Flatpaks, each with its own source
concepts.note: One list, several package systems; Trier Bridge always shows which system owns a program.

concepts.title: Default Apps
concepts.linux: Per-user MIME associations (mimeapps.list) via GNOME Settings

concepts.title: Settings
concepts.note: Same purpose; categories are organized differently. Trier Bridge routes familiar names to the right panel.

concepts.title: Printers
concepts.linux: CUPS through the GNOME Settings Printers panel

concepts.title: Power options
concepts.note: Power profiles replace power plans; sleep and lid settings live in the same panel.

concepts.title: Personalization
concepts.note: Wallpaper and light/dark style live here; full theming is a desktop-specific feature.

concepts.title: User accounts
concepts.note: Linux accounts are managed by the system; administrator rights come from group membership.

concepts.title: Date and time
concepts.linux: GNOME Settings System panel, Date & Time (timedated)

concepts.title: Language and region
concepts.linux: GNOME Settings System panel, Region & Language

concepts.title: Accessibility
concepts.linux: GNOME Settings Accessibility panel (Orca screen reader, zoom, high contrast)

concepts.title: Privacy
concepts.note: Per-app permissions apply to sandboxed apps; classic apps are governed by Linux permissions.

concepts.title: Windows Update
concepts.linux: Software Updater and the App Center (apt and snap)
concepts.note: System and application updates come through the package systems, with no forced restarts.

concepts.title: Network locations
concepts.note: Shares are opened as locations, not mapped to drive letters; Files can remember them as bookmarks.

concepts.title: Removable drives
concepts.linux: Mounted removable media (udisks2) shown in GNOME Files

concepts.title: Screenshot
concepts.linux: The GNOME screenshot tool (Print Screen); Trier Bridge opens the same tool through the desktop portal

concepts.title: Clipboard
concepts.linux: Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V work the same in apps; in the terminal use Ctrl+Shift+C and Ctrl+Shift+V. Clipboard history needs an extension.
concepts.note: Terminal shortcuts differ; there is no built-in clipboard history.

concepts.title: Registry Editor
concepts.linux: There is no registry. Settings live in files and in dconf/gsettings for the desktop.
concepts.note: No direct equivalent; nothing to open. Trier Bridge will not simulate one.

concepts.title: Task Scheduler
concepts.note: Scheduling exists (timers, cron) but has no graphical manager in this build.

concepts.title: Safe Mode
concepts.linux: Recovery mode from the boot menu (GRUB)
concepts.note: Recovery mode is chosen at boot; it is not started from inside the session.
